description: issue #685 (slice I6): registration is not invocation, and a click is host input — a headless batch `execute()` run has no pointer device, so an `on_click [ ... ]` handler is registered (emitting the `instruction`+`primitive` pair, seq 0-1) but never fires. This mirrors I3's `when "stop"` and I5's `on_key` narrowing: the following `print "mid"` runs (seq 2-3) and that is the whole event stream — `"moved"` is never printed. This slice deliberately did NOT synthesize a synthetic click-injection API to make the handler fire. Description reconciled by #688 (terminal slice): that later host slice HAS since landed — #686/I7 added `ExecuteOptions.hostInput`, so a click scheduled at a tick DOES fire every registered handler (see the sibling `on-click-handlers-fire-in-registration-order`), the same reconciliation #686 already applied to `on-click-wait-does-not-fire`. What this fixture pins is therefore narrower and still exactly true: with NO host input supplied, the pending-click queue is empty, so registration alone never fires the body. Locking that narrowing here makes it falsifiable rather than silently omitted.
